- When sentiment is negative and price is falling, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast dip depth.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots upward — cap forecast peak at 1–2% above true peak.
- If sentiment is strongly positive and price is trending up, model underestimates upside — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast.
- Model consistently underestimates short-term volatility in sentiment-driven corrections — increase forecast variance by 10–20% during sentiment swings.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model shows persistent downward bias — adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.0% to counteract mean reversion.
- Forecast horizon 30d often lags true price by 2–5 days — shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending strongly.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., negative → positive → negative), model fails to anticipate — apply smoothing filter to reduce overfitting to recent sentiment.
